plants.name: Chrysanthemum × morifolium
plants.description: A bushy perennial cultivated for its dense, layered flower heads in a huge range of forms, from pompons to spiders. It is among the last garden flowers to bloom in the Northern Hemisphere, tolerating cool autumn nights and light frosts.
plants.bloomingSeason: Autumn to early winter in the Northern Hemisphere (October to December)
plants.location: Cultivated worldwide; especially popular in East Asia, Europe, and North America
plants.funFact: Chrysanthemums are a symbol of the Japanese Imperial family, and the Chrysanthemum Throne is named for them. Flowering is triggered by the shortening days of autumn, as they are short-day plants.

plants.name: Jacaranda mimosifolia
plants.description: A large, graceful tree with fern-like leaves that erupts into clouds of lavender-blue trumpet-shaped flowers. When the blooms drop, they carpet streets and gardens in purple.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring to early summer in the Southern Hemisphere (October to December)
plants.location: Native to South America; widely planted in Australia, South Africa, and Argentina
plants.funFact: In Pretoria, South Africa, known as the Jacaranda City, tens of thousands of trees bloom in November. In Australia, an old tradition says that if a jacaranda flower falls on your head, you will pass your exams.

plants.name: Camellia sasanqua
plants.description: An evergreen shrub with glossy dark leaves and delicate, slightly fragrant single or semi-double flowers. It blooms earlier than the common camellia and brightens gardens as other plants fade.
plants.bloomingSeason: Autumn to early winter (October to January)
plants.location: Native to southern Japan; grown in the southeastern United States, Europe, and Australia
plants.funFact: The leaves of the related Camellia sinensis give us tea, and sasanqua seeds are pressed to make camellia oil used in cooking and cosmetics.

plants.name: Euphorbia pulcherrima
plants.description: A shrub whose colorful display comes from bracts, modified leaves surrounding tiny yellow flowers. In frost-free climates it grows into a large landscape shrub, and elsewhere it is a popular potted holiday plant.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late autumn to winter (November to February)
plants.location: Native to Mexico and Central America; grown worldwide as an ornamental
plants.funFact: The Aztecs called it cuetlaxochitl and used it to make a reddish dye and to treat fevers. Like chrysanthemums, poinsettias need long nights to develop their color.
